description: I'm Sourav Garai, a first-year B.Tech student in AI and Cybersecurity at The Neotia University. I turn ideas into working web applications, AI tools, chatbots and automation systems, using AI-assisted development to bring them to life. I enjoy taking on ambitious problems, learning through building and improving my projects through real testing. My focus is simple: build useful technology, keep learning and turn curiosity into something people can actually use.
summary: Mars Survival Map helps a future crew choose where humans first live on Mars - a survival decision about water, terrain, shelter, and radiation. The page opens on a real-texture 3D Mars globe with four marked candidate sites - Jezero Crater, Gale Crater, Valles Marineris, and Arcadia Planitia - and switches with one tap to a 2D science map layering NASA Mars Trek's Viking MDIM2.1 mosaic, MGS MOLA topography, and the USGS global geologic map, fetched live from official endpoints. Each site card shows only sourced, published evidence: ice detections, elevation, geology, and Curiosity RAD radiation measurements. A Crew Safety Index condenses that evidence into 0-100 scores that are honestly labeled as indicative - heuristic judgments from the evidence, not published measurements or validated safety guidance. A safety panel adds the measured Gale Crater dose rate (0.64 mSv/day) and today's solar activity from NASA's DONKI catalog. Everything is free and open: one static page, no paid APIs.
details: Mars Survival Map helps a future crew choose where humans first live on Mars - a survival decision about water, terrain, shelter, and radiation. The page opens on a real-texture 3D Mars globe (Three.js, CC BY 4.0 texture) with four marked candidate sites - Jezero Crater, Gale Crater, Valles Marineris, Arcadia Planitia - and switches with one tap to a 2D science map (Leaflet) layering NASA Mars Trek's Viking MDIM2.1 mosaic, MGS MOLA topography, and the USGS global geologic map, fetched live from official endpoints. Each site card shows only sourced, published evidence: ice detections, elevation, geology, and Curiosity RAD radiation measurements (Hassler et al. 2014). A Crew Safety Index condenses the evidence into 0-100 scores, honestly labeled as indicative heuristic judgments from that evidence - not published measurements or a validated safety model; a priority picker re-ranks the sites live. A safety panel adds the measured Gale Crater dose rate (0.64 mSv/day) and today's solar activity from NASA's DONKI catalog, labeled as solar context, not a live Mars radiation meter. Intended impact: anyone can compare real candidate landing sites on real NASA data in seconds and see the trade-offs honestly. Everything is free and open - one static page on GitHub Pages, no paid APIs. SI disclosure: an AI assistant proposed the four candidate sites and implemented the build; the human team member chose the combine-all-four concept and directed the work. All data values come from the cited NASA/USGS sources; the index scores are the AI's heuristic choices from that evidence, not astronaut safety guidance. Sources: trek.nasa.gov/mars (MDIM2.1, MOLA), astrogeology.usgs.gov (SIM 3292), ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/tools/DONKI, swim.psi.edu, doi:10.1126/science.1244797.
